qs.q:
Schooltime — Which person…

A=Alexander (hated school, bullied, poor family same clothes, French teacher called him stupid, physics teacher favourite)
B=Bethany (strict teachers, cheated in tests, extra home lessons, wishes she could go back)
C=Callum (lived for breaks/playtime, cooked meals at school, parents felt he could do better)
D=Daisy (not expected to stay on, couldn't stand school food, PE best, English teacher favourite)
E=Edward (school kept him off streets, no neighbourhood friends, school play, football Saturdays, left at 16)
F=Freya (rebel clique, cheated massively, dress code restrictions, didn't want school to end)

0. had parents who were not rich? [A=Alexander: 'because my parents were poor']
1. was good at sport?
2. felt he/she disappointed his/her parents?
3. disliked school meals?
4. disliked a subject because of the teacher?
5. was sorry to leave school?
6. felt under pressure to cheat?
7. enjoyed playtime most?
8. went to a school with a strict dress code?
9. wanted to leave school as soon as he/she could?
10. did not have friends at school?
11. would like to go to school again?
12. was a teacher's favourite?
items: 4 — disliked a subject because of the teacher?
8 — went to a school with a strict dress code?
9 — wanted to leave school as soon as he/she could?
10 — did not have friends at school?
11 — would like to go to school again?

qs.q:
Going for a Swim

"My parents just didn't see learning as a priority, despite the fact that... there was hardly a lack of swimming facilities in our town."

The author believes he didn't learn to swim at an early age because…
A the sea where he lived was too rough.
B he was too afraid of getting into water.
C there were no local swimming pools.
D his parents were not interested in him learning.
opts: the sea where he lived was too rough.
he was too afraid of getting into water.
there were no local swimming pools.
his parents were not interested in him learning.

qs.q:
Going for a Swim

"I can't say I felt any embarrassment about it... I wasn't all that bothered."

How did the author feel about being in the group for those unable to swim?
A He was ashamed.
B He did not care.
C He felt unconfident.
D He became more determined.

Going for a Swim

"I changed and fell in with a different crowd who were into other things and thought that swimming was as dull as it was uncool."

Why did the author give up swimming?
A He thought it was boring.
B He had stopped making progress.
C He went to live in another town.
D He gave into peer pressure.
opts: He went to live in another town.

qs.q:
Going for a Swim

"The constant pleading of my fiancée forced me to give in and try the water."

What made the author take up swimming again?
A The beautiful Greek sea.
B Pressure from his girlfriend.
C The unbearable heat on holiday.
D A need to lose weight.

Going for a Swim

"I hadn't expected that it wouldn't be part of the physical education curriculum, so we invested in a course."

What surprised the author when he wanted his children to learn to swim?
A The fact that there were no swimming lessons at school.
B How quickly they were able to learn how to swim.
C The price he had to pay for the swimming lessons.
D How much they enjoyed themselves when swimming.
opts: The fact that there were no swimming lessons at school.
How quickly they were able to learn how to swim.
The price he had to pay for the swimming lessons.
How much they enjoyed themselves when swimming.

Don't get rid of citizenship education

"Too many teachers of the subject were not specialists and had not received sufficient training. (19) ___. And this year, education secretary Michael Gove indicated that the subject may no longer be compulsory."

A However, citizenship education should not be limited to schools.
B The removal of citizenship education takes away one of the few ways the state can encourage such behaviour.
C In this way, they are more likely to make a positive contribution to their communities.
D Meanwhile, the handful of enthusiastic citizenship teachers found their subject given little status by their colleagues.
E The teaching methods encourage students to form their own opinions.
F These are strong arguments against abandoning citizenship education.
G Yet too many British adults struggle to understand this country's politics.
H Instead of doing away with citizenship education, we should be starting it earlier.
opts: A — citizenship education should not be limited to schools
B — removal takes away one of few ways state can encourage such behaviour
C — they are more likely to make positive contribution
D — the handful of enthusiastic teachers found their subject given little status
E — teaching methods encourage students to form their own opinions
F — these are strong arguments against abandoning citizenship education
G — yet too many British adults struggle to understand this country's politics
H — instead of doing away with it, we should start it earlier
